tagline: Application delivery and security solutions for hybrid multicloud environments
hero_kpi_rationale: Key indicator reflecting product base growth (systems and software), with an 18.5% YoY increase driven by customer demand and improved product mix in hybrid multicloud environments
company_description: F5, Inc. provides multicloud application security and delivery solutions in the United States, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia Pacific region. The company's distributed cloud services enable its customers to deploy, secure, and operate applications in any architecture, from on-premises to the public cloud. It also offers unified, security, networking, and application management solutions, such as web app and API protection; multi-cloud networking; application delivery and deployment; domain name system; content delivery network; and application deployment and orchestration. In addition, the company provides application security and delivery products, including NGINX Plus; NGINX One Console; NGINX Ingress Controller; WAF for NGINX; BIG-IP Packaged Software; and BIG-IP Systems. Further, it provides a range of professional services, including maintenance, consulting, training, and other technical support services. The company sells its products to large enterprise businesses, public sector institutions, governments, and service providers through distributors, value-added resellers, managed service providers, systems integrators, and other indirect channel partners. risks.title: Nation-state cyberattack
risks.summary: A sophisticated nation-state actor accessed BIG-IP source code, threatening product security and customer trust.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned in the first part of the risk factors with very strong language (nation-state threat actor, long-term persistent access). The exfiltration of BIG-IP source code and undisclosed vulnerabilities constitutes a potential existential threat to customer trust. The text indicates anticipated impacts on sales cycles and operating margin in 2026, which reinforces the severity. The cybersecurity category is highly critical in the IT sector.

risks.title: Post-cyber incident sales cycle disruption
risks.summary: The cyber incident has slowed sales, particularly at the beginning of fiscal year 2026, due to distrust or deferred purchasing decisions.
risks.score_rationale: The text explicitly indicates an anticipation of near-term disruption to our sales cycles with a stronger impact at the beginning of fiscal year 2026. The language is clear and forward-looking, showing a direct consequence of the cyber incident. Although temporary, this affects growth and competitiveness against competitors. The competition category is heavily weighted here because the risk relates to loss of market share or deals.

risks.title: Dependence on macroeconomic demand
risks.summary: Global economic uncertainty, with inflation and high interest rates, weighs on customer investment decisions.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is repeated in multiple sections with significant language (uncertain economic conditions, inflation, tariffs, higher interest rates). It is linked to customer demand stability, particularly sensitive for Fortune 1000 companies. Compared to the previous year, the tone is more cautious, indicating a perceived worsening of the risk. The macro category is critical for enterprise IT solution sales.

risks.title: Revenue concentration on two distributors
risks.summary: A large share of revenues depends on only two distributors, creating a commercial imbalance risk.
risks.score_rationale: Two distributors alone account for 33.3% of revenues (15.8% and 17.5%). The risk is stable compared to the previous year, but dependence remains high. The text does not show notable improvement or diversification. The loss of a single partner would have a significant impact on distribution. The competition category is chosen because this affects negotiating power and resilience against competitors.

risks.title: Evolution of software consumption models
risks.summary: The transition to SaaS and subscription models changes revenue recognition and requires continuous adaptation.
risks.score_rationale: The shift from perpetual licenses to subscription and SaaS is mentioned as a factor that may affect revenue timing and classification. The language is cautious but recurring, particularly in the Critical Accounting Estimates section. This risk is stable but structural, linked to digital transformation. The technology category is moderately weighted, but critical for revenue predictability.

risks.title: Pressure on product margins
risks.summary: Product margins are under pressure due to manufacturing costs, components, and obsolete inventory.
risks.score_rationale: Product gross margin decreased from 28.1% in 2023 to 22.4% in 2025, despite partial improvement in 2025. The text cites factors such as material costs, component price increases, and supply constraints. Although partially offset by a more favorable mix, margin pressure persists. The risk is stable but significant for profitability. The capital category reflects the impact on cash generation.

risks.title: Increased expenses related to cyber incident
risks.summary: Additional expenses are expected in 2026 to address the consequences of the cyber incident.
risks.score_rationale: The company anticipates incurring additional professional and other fees in 2026 related to incident response. Although deemed not material at this stage, they are anticipated to recur in the following fiscal year. The language is measured but forward-looking. The capital category is relevant as this affects operating cash flow. The risk is new but of moderate intensity.
